newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK seen earning $32 mln from handover visitors.
newsitem.headline: HK seen earning $32 mln from handover visitors.

text.p: Hong Kong's hotels, restaurants and shops stand to see a windfall of HK$250 million (US$32 million) from the 8,300 visitors expected for the British colony's handover to China, the government said on Wednesday.

"Assuming that 8,300 additional visitors will stay in Hong Kong for an average of 10 days and these visitors will spend, on average, HK$3,000 per day, their total net additional spending is estimated at around HK$250 million," Acting Secretary for Economic Services, Leo Kwan, told the local legislature.
Kwan said HK$3,000 was approximately the average spending of visitors staying in four-star hotels.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese sovereignty at midnight on June 30 after more than 150 years of British rule.
"All the hotel rooms in Hong Kong are expected to be occupied during that period," Kwan said.
Tourism was the second largest foreign exchange earner for Hong Kong in 1995, with visitor spending totalling HK$72 billion or about six percent of the territory's gross domestic product.
In the first eight months of 1996, the latest figures available, 7.53 million people visited Hong Kong, an increase of 16.2 percent from the same period the year before.
